parsed_action.body: The next phase must advance only mechanisms that earned local roles, not untested general architectures. The current program has validated exact external custody [S09], deterministic first-fit relief under narrow pressure [S10], and host-owned response/control reserves [S02]. It has not validated model-owned eviction, automatic phase discovery, artifact coupling as a general mechanism, or a unified architecture for bounded agents [S14]. The decision is to proceed with an interaction-first roadmap that tests joint effects of ingress bandwidth and cumulative work externalization, while maintaining strict stopping rules and candidate-bound evaluation [S02][S13]. Scope excludes broad applicability claims beyond the tested pressure boundaries and model configurations [S10]. This scope explicitly rejects claiming that artifact coupling, notes, digests, progress state, model-owned eviction, automatic phase discovery, or a general architecture is already validated. The program must distinguish mechanisms that earned a role from those that were only behaviorally active, locally harmful, blocked, or still untested [S04][S08]. The boundary between earned and untested mechanisms is critical: exact custody is earned because both arms maintain identical external objects; relief is qualified because it operates under narrow pressure boundaries; and host ownership is earned because manager and paging results support it. In contrast, model-owned eviction remains untested, automatic phase discovery has no local validation, and artifact coupling has not demonstrated general utility beyond specific runs [S02][S14].
parsed_action.heading: Decision and scope
